findings.title: Blindness carried into path loss
findings.claim: The focus's repeated blindness can be read as a carried failure of recognition whose later result is loss of the way; the wider echoes allow its sensory mode to change while the route-loss remains.
findings.mechanism: The two أَعْمَىٰ predicates meet wider scenes that locate blindness in hearts rather than eyes (22:46), relate blindness to the Hereafter itself (27:66), and connect turning from remembrance to being gathered blind (20:124). The covering of hearts and weight in ears at 17:46 supplies a possible obstruction to receiving the message. At the focus's أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا, 25:34 repeats the greater path-straying in a face-first gathering and 42:46 describes the straying person as having no way; this contact makes the comparative a route-finding failure rather than only a degree. The question in 20:125 leaves a bodily shift from former sight live alongside cognitive blindness.
findings.reader_payoff: More astray as to the way becomes a loss of the capacity to find or reach a route, while the repeated blindness can carry across domains without requiring one unchanged sensory mode.
findings.containment: The locative فِي ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ remains the focus wording: 27:66 offers an adjacent blindness-about-the-Hereafter relation, not a grammatical replacement. 20:125 explicitly contrasts prior sight with being gathered blind, so the continuity reading does not require an unchanged cognitive or bodily state. Cognitive and literal-sensory readings remain live together.

epistemic.reason: The citable trusted cross-run record anchors the focus branches, while a legacy walk only corroborates them. Wider connections supply exact target Arabic but explicitly omit target morphology and lexical analysis; the unknown-terrain activation is analogical and 20:125 preserves a live modality contrast.
